_comment: Ground truth for pr-review-beat.jsonl, hand-written. ONE statement: the demo corrects the button colour on the standing prop PR sharique2004/adjourn#6 ('[demo-prop] Add join button to landing page'). Loaded verbatim by extraction.load_fixture_statements('pr-review-beat'). See PR_REVIEW_PROP.md in this directory for the prop, the spoken line, and the between-rehearsals reset.
_stage_2_closed: EntityReferences carries pr_topic / old_value / new_value, so pr_topic 'join button' and new_value '#6b7f99' ride in entity_refs and survive load_fixture_statements(). planner.build_pr_review_suggestion routes them to kind 'pr_review_suggestion' and suppresses the github_update that used to carry this beat. old_value stays absent by design and is derived from the diff at execution time.

statements.speaker: You
statements.claim: The join button on PR #6 should use the team's slate blue #6b7f99 instead of the green it currently ships.
statements.quote: Yeah, the copy's fine. But on Priya's join button PR — pull six — that green is wrong. It should be our slate blue, six B seven F nine nine.
statements._comment: kind is 'decision' because ROUTING_TABLE maps decision -> github_update and this beat is a plan being reversed, not an assignment or a deadline; planner.build_pr_review_suggestion then takes it and SUPPRESSES that github_update. Both entity_refs are spoken IN prb-s05, per the rule in fixtures/README.md: 'pull six' gives issue_number 6 (GitHub numbers PRs and issues in one space, so a spoken pull number is an issue_number), and 'Priya's' gives person. person is safe on a decision — planner._describe_change only reads person when kind == 'assignment', so this cannot render a spurious 'owner X -> Y' diff. The number is rewritten by adjourn.tools.seed_demo_world.sync_fixtures whenever the prop is rebuilt; do not hand-edit it.
statements._claim_note: The claim deliberately does NOT name the old hex. #2ecc71 is nowhere in the transcript — it is only in the PR's diff. Writing it into the claim would make this ground truth unreachable for a live extraction run, which sees the words and not the code, and the whole point of the fixture floor is that it describes a CORRECT reading of the transcript. The old value is recorded under _extras with its provenance marked, and reading it is the reviewer's job, not the extractor's.

_extras._convention: Stage-2 payload for the PR-review action. DROPPED by Statement.from_dict — documentation and test input only, never runtime data. When EntityReferences grows real fields, these are the names to use.
_extras.new_value_spoken_as: six B seven F nine nine

statements._stage_2_closed_note: old_value is still absent from entity_refs and that is still correct — '#2ecc71' is nowhere in the transcript. It is no longer a gap, though: pr_review_suggestion_executor.derive_old_value reads it out of the PR's diff, accepting the answer only when the diff adds exactly one colour. So the inline suggestion fires without anyone reading a hex code aloud.
